page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-48GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.0 GB of memory per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does include one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The server utilizes a shared CPU allocation model, which introduces specific performance tradeoffs. In synthetic benchmarks, the stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 10%, reflecting the shared nature of the resources. However, multi-core and memory benchmarks demonstrate more balanced capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core performance, PassMark CPU score of 28502.96, and Geekbench multi-core score of 14914.0 all fall within average ranges. Notably, Geekbench single-core, image processing, and text processing benchmarks show strong performance, placing in the top 25%.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server is positioned as a cost-efficient option for workloads that require high core counts and moderate memory without constant, sustained peak CPU utilization. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, text processing, static web serving, and moderate database operations. It can also handle light LLM inference tasks, achieving 10.52 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model.
